title: Blackbody Radiation
body:
A **blackbody** is an object that absorbs all light falling on it and re-emits according to its
temperature alone. Stars are close enough to one for the two laws below to apply.

**Wien's law** puts the peak of the emission at

$$
\lambda_{max} = \frac{2.9 \times 10^{-3}}{T} \text{ metres}
$$

```
T = 10,000 K   ->   290 nm    ultraviolet, and the star looks blue-white
T =  5,800 K   ->   500 nm    visible, the Sun
T =  3,000 K   ->   966 nm    infrared, and the star looks red
```

Hotter is bluer, which turns a star's colour into a thermometer requiring no contact and no
distance measurement.

**The Stefan-Boltzmann law** gives the energy radiated per unit area as $\sigma T^4$, so
doubling the temperature multiplies the output per square metre by 16. Combined with surface
area, the total luminosity is

$$
L = 4\pi R^2 \sigma T^4
$$

Both quantities matter, which is what makes the [[HR Diagram]] two-dimensional. A red
giant is cool and enormously luminous because it is vast, and a [[White Dwarf]] is hot and
dim because it is tiny, and the two laws are what separate them.
